items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I worked with his orchestra for a short while. When he hit the Fin egan book, and he asked me to go out on the road with him

ctx.x: his association with Benny Goodman. Benny Goodman's entrance into the jazz picture from '35 on, I only mention this -- not to deviate from my personal story, but because all of us drummers in the jazz era were affected in some way of another by his predominance. A legend in his time, without peer.

I mention Ray McKinley, a great drummer, whom I heard with the Dorsey brothers around '32 or '33. I heard him a couple of times in person on one nighters, and in Massachusetts and then back in my home town on the radio from Glen Island Casino -- I loved the sound of his drums, Ray McKinley. Here is tuning again -- his intense, but loose swinging beat and taste behind soloists. He's one of the masters of his time and through the years, a veteran swinger. He and I were also friends. I'm beginning to sound like…

Well, it turned out that I did all the vocalists; Ray directed and did the vocalists, but when it came time to clear the swinging drum parts, Ray used to come back and say I've got it, Cliff. But however, he's a dear friend, and we shall remain that way.
